title: A clearer way to read the evidence
subtitle: A report should make its strongest finding easy to see, then give the evidence room to breathe. This sample demonstrates reading flow, not a factual research result.

blocks.title: Make the first reading useful
paragraphs: Readers often enter a report through a headline, a chart, or a number. A clear hierarchy lets them understand the main point before choosing where to read more deeply.

Two columns can support sustained reading when line lengths remain comfortable. They are continuous text columns: the reader follows one column before continuing into the next. This is different from a main column with an independent sidebar.
Wide evidence needs space. A chart that carries several comparisons should span the text columns, while a caption and source note stay close to the graphic.

blocks.text: The evidence needs enough space to remain legible.

blocks.title: Use emphasis with restraint
paragraphs: A large-number callout works best when only a few values deserve special attention. The next section should explain the same information rather than introduce another row of equally dominant cards.
This composition is deliberately quieter around the body text. Display type, paragraph spacing, shared alignment lines, and a small accent color establish a predictable rhythm.

blocks.title: Image and text share one reading unit
paragraphs: The visual occupies one side, and a short explanation occupies the other. On a small screen, the figure precedes its explanation.
The caption names the image. Supplied provenance remains below the illustration instead of becoming an unreadable footer.
